title.narrative: Nourish to Survive: Emergency Nutrition Response for Vulnerable Populations in Bama, Gwoza (Pulka) and Monguno LGAs

description.narrative: ltpgtIn northeast Nigeria, protracted conflict and displacement have severely disrupted food systems, health services, and livelihoods, leaving vulnerable populations, especially children under five and pregnant/lactating women, at heightened risk of malnutrition and preventable death. In Borno State, the LGAs of Bama, Gwoza (Pulka), and Monguno remain among the most critically affected, with alarming nutrition indicators and limited access to life-saving services. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRecent nutrition surveillance data reveals Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates exceeding the emergency threshold of 15% in these locations, with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) prevalence ranging between 3.5% to 6.1%. In Monguno LGA, SMART Survey report conducted by PUI in June 2024 showed a GAM rate of 26.7% and SAM of 6.1%, In Gwoza LGA, the GAM rate was reported at 35.1% and in Bama LGA, 15.9% (OCHA, 2024). Compounded by poor WASH conditions, disease outbreaks, and food insecurity, the risk of excess mortality is high without urgent intervention. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis project aims to deliver emergency preventive nutrition response through community-based nutrition approach specifically through supplemental nutrition assistant through Tom Brown and Maternal Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN). The following results are expected: ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtltspangt14,444 Children under the age of five years will be screened for Malnutrition. Depending on the status of their malnutrition, they will be referred to case management service delivery points (OTP, SC or MAM program)lt/spangtlt/ligtltligt2,880 children under five MAM will be treated through TSFP/Tom Brown approach. lt/ligtltligt1,755 pregnant and lactating women (PLW)/care givers including men will be reached with Behavior change communication to promote optimal infant and young child feeding (IYCF) practices. lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtltbrgtFollowing Nutrition Cluster, MOH and local health authorities' standards, the project will deploy community nutrition volunteers to strengthen and scale up community active case search and referral of under-five malnourished children to MAM, OTP or SC program. By addressing acute malnutrition in early stage, the intervention will reduce morbidity and mortality, build community resilience, and contribute directly to humanitarian and sectoral objectives. lt/pgt
